note: Blank filtering and the usable floor, independent of binning. Expected values are hand-derived from the rules. medianLength uses the mean of the two middle values for an even-length list, and the comparison is `length >= (pct/100) * median` — a frame exactly on the threshold is kept.

cases.name: drops frames below the threshold
cases.why: median is 10750; 15% of it is 1612.5, so 500 and 400 go and nothing else does

cases.name: threshold is relative, not absolute
cases.why: same shape as the case above at a tenth the scale. An absolute byte threshold would delete the whole episode; a median-relative one travels to content encoded at different settings

cases.name: floor: a uniformly tiny episode is not gutted
cases.why: every frame is near the median so none is blank — the filter is a no-op here and the floor is never reached. Included because it is the case people expect to fail

cases.name: floor: relaxes rather than returning almost nothing
cases.why: median is 100 so the six small frames pass and the three large ones do too — nothing is below 15 bytes. The point of the case is that a lopsided distribution does not accidentally delete the majority

cases.name: a single frame survives
cases.why: the floor cannot invent frames; minUsable is a target, not a promise
